why: Quote is verbatim (troubleshooting.md:113), but the finding names the wrong subsystem and its consequence is false one layer up. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The doc scopes the knob in its own section opener at :77 -- 'If the Search tool, `@file` mentions, custom agents, or custom skills aren't finding files' -- and the second half of the very line quoted confirms it: 'run `claude doctor` ... and check that the Search line'. All of those are the AGENT's file-discovery surfaces inside the Claude Code process. The cited `resolveRipgrepPath` (runtime-resolver.ts:442) feeds only `packages/server-core/src/services/search.ts` -> `searchSessions`, which is the desktop shell's session-HISTORY full-text search: it greps `-g '**/session.jsonl'` under the sessions dir for transcript text. Claude Code has no session-history search feature at all, so USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP was never its knob. This is exactly the disallowed-tools-for-subagents-vs-skills trap. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE UPSTREAM. For the surface the doc IS about, the fork already honours the variable, by inheritance rather than by code of ours. The Claude backend runs the real Claude Agent SDK subprocess, and `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-243) builds its env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides}` -- an open passthrough that deletes only three Bedrock vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL). A user who exports USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 before launching gets it into the SDK subprocess, which implements the documented switch. The repo states this design explicitly for a sibling SDK knob at claude-agent.ts:310-318: MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES 'reaches the subprocess by env inheritance -- deliberately NOT renamed on the Claude side (the Nessy Pi loop has its own NESSY_-prefixed knob)'. So 0 repo hits for USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP is the CORRECT state, not a gap: the variable belongs to the SDK we embed, and re-implementing it here would be the defect. (3) THE CITED CODE IS MISREAD. The claim of 'three fixed candidates ... and consults no environment variable' undercounts: lines 457-466 add a FOURTH, resolving system `rg` from PATH via which/where whenever `!hostRuntime.isPackaged` (headless server, dev mode) -- i.e. the non-packaged host already does what the doc asks, without a flag. The packaged exclusion is a stated deliberate decision in the same comment: 'Packaged apps must use vendored binary only -- never resolve from PATH to avoid picking up an incompatible system install.' (4) 'DEAD WITH NO USER-REACHABLE RECOVERY' IS OVERSTATED. SearchUnavailableError is caught in apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionSearch.ts:352-357, which sets isSearchUnavailable; SessionList.tsx:723 forwards it and SessionSearchHeader.tsx:99 renders the localized `session.searchUnavailable` notice. Only CONTENT search degrades -- title/name filtering is a separate non-ripgrep path and keeps working -- and the failure is surfaced, not silent. Also checked: this is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) -- it is refuted on subsystem and consequence, not on a recorded decision.
correctedState: No divergence. The documented recovery applies to the Claude Code agent's own file discovery (Search tool, @file, agents, skills), and the fork preserves it unchanged: `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-243) spreads `...process.env` into the Claude Agent SDK subprocess, stripping only three Bedrock routing vars, so an exported USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 reaches the SDK and takes effect. Zero repo hits is correct by design -- the same env-inheritance rule the repo records for MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES at claude-agent.ts:310-318. The cited `resolveRipgrepPath` (runtime-resolver.ts:442) serves a DIFFERENT, Nessy-only subsystem with no Claude Code counterpart: session-history full-text search over session.jsonl (server-core/src/services/search.ts). Even there the claim is inaccurate -- a fourth candidate at :457-466 resolves system `rg` from PATH for non-packaged hosts, packaged builds exclude PATH by a stated in-code decision, and failure surfaces to the user as `session.searchUnavailable` (SessionSearchHeader.tsx:99) while title search continues.
